name: TinyShelf

sources.title: TinyShelf homepage — 'tiny, curated directory of good software', every listing reviewed
Submit page — redirects to Google OAuth sign-in

requirements: Google account required — /submit redirects straight to a Google OAuth sign-in; no other auth provider shown
Human curation: 'Every listing is reviewed before it goes live'

Broad software taxonomy accepted — categories from Productivity and AI/ML to CLI Tools, Databases, Editors/IDEs; tags mark platform (iOS/Mac/Android/Windows/Linux/browser-extension) and pricing model (free/freemium/subscription/one-time/open-source/self-hosted)
preparation: Tool name, URL, one-line description, category and tags
workflow: Sign in with Google (OAuth consent screen — app name tinyshelf.co)
Listing is held for human review, then appears under categories/tags and the 'newest tools' feed
watchFor: OAuth consent shows the operator's personal Gmail — hobby-scale directory; review turnaround may vary
No pricing page, badge requirement, or paid tier visible anywhere on the public site
Curated means rejection is possible — thin/low-quality submissions likely declined
countsAsLive: The tool has a public page at tinyshelf.co/tools/<slug> reachable from its category and tag pages.
unknowns: Submit-form fields behind the Google sign-in
Review latency and rejection criteria detail
Whether the free model is permanent (no monetization surface visible)
